observations: Photo 0 shows two stacked automatic transmission units, heavily oxidized, with torque-converter bell housings visible, sitting on a dirty workshop floor among other scrap parts.
Photo 1 is a close-up of a transmission case with loose bare wires (red, blue, orange) twisted together near a connector, no visible plug housing properly seated.
Photo 2 shows another gearbox unit with hoses and brackets still attached, a pink paint dab on the casing, sitting next to unrelated engine/alternator parts.
No printed part number, VIN tag, or model plate is legible in any photo.
No vehicle, odometer, or test-rig context is shown to support 'tested and working' or 'low mileage' claims.
Rust and grime on mating surfaces suggest the units have been sitting removed for some time, not freshly pulled.

response.reason: The photos show a genuine used Toyota-type automatic/manual gearbox but with no readable model number, no proof of testing, and a loose wiring issue that raises doubt about electrical integrity, so it must be priced at worst case as an unverified, possibly faulty used gearbox core comparable to other gearbox-only (not engine+gearbox) Toyota listings.
